tasks.short: Work out costs of packaging, pallets, fuel and overhead from supplier quotes and price lists for cost checks and recharges.

today.trigger: A supplier quote, new price list or cost recharge question from a site manager or the Controller.
steps: Open the quote or price list (PDF or Excel attachment in Outlook)
Copy prices into an Excel costing sheet
Add overhead and surcharge rates (fuel, indexation) from last year's sheet
Compare with what AFAS shows was paid before
Send the result to the requester or post a recharge in AFAS
drudgery: Retyping prices from PDFs
Hunting for the latest overhead rates
Checking units (per pallet, per km, per hour) by hand
today.time_sinks: Retyping and reconciling units across quotes; finding the right previous price in AFAS.

lenses.faster: An LLM step reads the quote into a price table and a fixed Excel or Power BI model applies overhead and surcharge rates; retyping and unit checks go.
lenses.autonomous: Each new price list mailed to the AP inbox is parsed and compared with the prices on the last 12 months of AFAS invoices, and increases above a threshold are flagged.
lenses.ambitious: Cost every supplier price change against actual volumes, so Finance sees the yearly effect of indexation and fuel surcharges before the contract is renewed.
lenses.joy: No more copying price lines from PDFs; what is left is asking why a price moved.
lenses.options: Show three costings side by side (current supplier, quoted, cheapest alternative from history) instead of one number.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper owns the overhead rates, unit conversions and price-change thresholds, not the arithmetic.
reach: FP&A Analyst: price-change input to the forecast
Controller: cost allocation checks across the three sites

tasks.human_edge: Knowing which quotes are binding, which surcharges were negotiated away, and when a number looks wrong for the site.
tasks.pattern_why: Quotes and price lists arrive as unstructured PDFs; extraction into a table is a model step, the costing itself is fixed rules and checkable.

in_practice.trigger: Quote or price list lands in the AP mailbox or a SharePoint folder.
steps: LLM extracts item, unit, price, validity and surcharges into a table
Rules normalise units and apply overhead rates from a maintained rate table
Compare against prices on AFAS invoices for the same supplier
Flag differences above the threshold and draft a short note
Bookkeeper checks and sends or posts
in_practice.human_gate: Bookkeeper approves every costing before it is sent or posted.
data_needed: AFAS invoice line history per supplier
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint costing log with source file, extracted table and approver

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit reads PDF and UBL documents to line level, which supplies the price history to compare against.
evidence.source: [S1] Irixs, AFAS Profit 8; [S2] AFAS Help Center, Scan & herken

evidence.claim: LLMs can extract price tables from supplier PDFs reliably enough for a checked workflow.

risks: Misread unit or currency gives a wrong costing that looks precise
Overhead rate table goes stale if nobody owns it
Quotes contain confidential terms; processing must stay inside the M365 tenant (AVG and contract confidentiality)
research_questions: How many quotes and price lists per month does AP actually cost, and how long does each take today?
What share of quote PDFs extract correctly to unit price without correction in a 50-document test?
Does AFAS invoice line data carry consistent units per supplier to compare against?

tasks.short: Match Rabobank statement lines to open invoices and ledger entries in AFAS, and chase what does not match.

today.trigger: Daily CAMT.053 bank statement import from Rabobank into AFAS.
steps: Import the bank statement into AFAS
Let AFAS match what it can
Work through unmatched lines one by one
Look up remittance details, emails or agency portals to find the invoice
Post to suspense or ask a colleague when unclear
drudgery: Searching for customers who pay several invoices in one amount without reference
Clearing small differences and bank charges by hand
Keeping the suspense account list in Excel
today.time_sinks: Unmatched lines with no or wrong payment reference, part payments and combined payments.

lenses.faster: Tighter AFAS match rules (reference, IBAN, invoice number, set tolerances) clear most lines; an LLM step proposes the match for leftovers using remittance text and email.
lenses.autonomous: Every morning the statement imports and matches itself; only lines without a confident match land in the bookkeeper's queue with a suggested invoice.
lenses.ambitious: Daily instead of weekly clean bank position, so the suspense account is empty at month end and the close starts a day earlier.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses ticking off 300 lines; what is left is the odd payment that needs a phone call.
lenses.options: For each unmatched line, show the top three candidate invoices with the reason for each.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper owns match rules and tolerances and reviews the unmatched rate weekly.
reach: Credit and Collections Officer: spotting part payments and disputes early
Controller: cash position for the month-end close

tasks.human_edge: Judging an ambiguous payment, knowing the customer, and deciding when to call rather than post to suspense.
tasks.pattern_why: Bank matching on reference, IBAN, invoice number and amount is rules on structured CAMT.053 data; AFAS already does it.

in_practice.trigger: CAMT.053 file available from Rabobank each morning.
steps: Auto-import into AFAS
Run AFAS match rules with agreed tolerances
LLM step proposes matches for leftover lines from remittance text and emails
Bookkeeper confirms or corrects proposals
Weekly report of match rate and reasons for misses
in_practice.human_gate: Bookkeeper confirms any match outside the rules and any posting to suspense or write-off.
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS bank statement audit trail plus a match-rule change log in SharePoint

evidence.claim: AFAS matches CAMT.053 lines on payment reference, IBAN, invoice number and oldest-first sums, exact unless a tolerance is set; misses go to a person.
An LLM can suggest matches from free-text remittance information.

risks: Too wide a tolerance hides short payments
Wrong auto-match on similar amounts misstates customer balances
Rules drift when customers change payment habits
research_questions: What is today's AFAS auto-match rate and what are the top five reasons for misses?
How much time per week goes to unmatched lines versus the import itself?
Would a small tolerance (e.g. EUR 1) clear bank-charge differences without hiding real short payments?

tasks.short: Pull AP, AR, cash and cost reports from AFAS into Excel tables for the Controller and site managers.

today.trigger: Weekly cash and ageing report, month-end close, or an ad-hoc question from the Controller or Finance Director.
steps: Export lists from AFAS (ageing, open items, cost per site)
Clean and pivot in Excel
Copy into last month's template
Add notes on large items
Mail or put on SharePoint
drudgery: Same export and pivot every week
Fixing broken formulas in inherited templates
Writing the same notes on recurring items
today.time_sinks: Re-building the same Excel tables each period and answering one-off variants of them.

lenses.faster: Standard reports move to Power BI on the nightly AFAS extract; the export-clean-pivot cycle disappears.
lenses.autonomous: Ageing, cash and AP reports refresh nightly and go out on a schedule; an LLM step drafts notes on the largest movements for review.
lenses.ambitious: Site managers get their own cost and open-item view per site each week instead of a monthly PDF.
lenses.joy: No more template repair; the work left is explaining what moved and why.
lenses.options: Offer the same data cut by site, customer group or supplier type without rebuilding the sheet.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper defines report definitions and data checks and answers questions the dashboard raises.
reach: FP&A Analyst: actuals feed for the forecast
Credit and Collections Officer: ageing and DSO view

tasks.human_edge: Knowing which numbers matter to which reader and catching data that is technically right but misleading.
tasks.pattern_why: Structured AFAS data, fixed report definitions and checkable totals; build once in Power BI.

in_practice.trigger: Nightly AFAS extract refresh and a fixed schedule.
steps: Power BI refreshes report pages on the AFAS extract
Totals reconcile automatically to the AFAS trial balance
LLM step drafts notes on movements above a threshold
Bookkeeper reviews notes and publishes
in_practice.human_gate: Bookkeeper approves the commentary before distribution; numbers publish automatically once reconciliation passes.
in_practice.logs_to: Power BI refresh history and a SharePoint publication log

evidence.claim: Noordhaven already runs Power BI on a nightly AFAS extract for finance dashboards.
Scheduled Power BI reports with automated distribution replace manual Excel report packs.

risks: Extract gaps (late postings) make reports look complete when they are not
LLM commentary states a cause that is not in the data
Access to supplier and customer detail must follow AVG role rules
research_questions: Which reports are produced each week and month, and how many hours do they take?
Does the nightly extract contain all fields (site, cost centre, due date) the reports need?
Do readers actually use the commentary, or only the tables?

tasks.short: Run the trial balance in AFAS at month end, check odd balances and suspense accounts, and fix postings.

today.trigger: Month-end close calendar from the Controller.
steps: Run the trial balance in AFAS
Export to Excel and compare with last month
Investigate accounts with unusual balances or signs
Clear suspense and interim accounts
Hand the checked balance to the Controller
drudgery: Comparing columns month on month by eye
Clearing interim accounts line by line
Chasing missing invoices before cut-off
today.time_sinks: Finding the cause of odd balances and waiting on missing documents.

lenses.faster: A fixed set of checks (sign, movement versus last month and budget, non-zero suspense, interim accounts) runs on the AFAS trial balance and lists only exceptions.
lenses.autonomous: The checks run daily during the last week of the month, so problems are fixed before day 1 of the close.
lenses.ambitious: A soft close every week, which cuts days to close and audit adjustments.
lenses.joy: No more column-by-column comparison; the job becomes solving the few real breaks.
lenses.options: Show each exception with likely causes ranked (missing accrual, wrong VAT code, misposting).
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper owns the check rules and thresholds with the Controller.

tasks.human_edge: Judging whether an odd balance is a real error or a known business event, and fixing it correctly.
tasks.pattern_why: Trial balance data is structured and the checks can be written as rules with checkable outcomes.

in_practice.trigger: Daily from close day -5, plus on demand.
steps: Pull the trial balance from AFAS
Run sign, movement, suspense and interim checks
LLM step writes a one-line likely cause for each exception
Bookkeeper fixes or routes each exception
Controller signs off the checked balance
in_practice.human_gate: Bookkeeper approves every correcting entry; Controller signs off the balance.
in_practice.logs_to: Close checklist in SharePoint with exceptions and resolutions

evidence.claim: Rule-based balance checks on ERP data are standard close tooling.
Booking proposals alone do not remove exceptions; own accounts and VAT codes keep requiring people.

risks: Thresholds set too loose hide errors that the auditor later finds
False exceptions train people to ignore the list
Fixing balances without root cause repeats each month
research_questions: How many audit adjustments last year came from errors a balance check would have caught?
How many hours per close go to trial balance review today?
Which accounts produce most exceptions, and are those fixable upstream?

tasks.short: Gather last year's actuals and cost estimates per site into the budget templates for FP&A.

today.trigger: Annual budget round and quarterly reforecast run by FP&A.
steps: Export actuals per site and cost centre from AFAS
Fill the budget templates in Excel
Collect estimates from site managers by email
Chase missing input
Hand the compiled file to FP&A
drudgery: Copying actuals into many templates
Chasing site managers for input
Merging versions
today.time_sinks: Waiting for and merging inputs from site managers.

lenses.faster: Templates prefill from AFAS actuals and known contracts; managers only edit changes.
lenses.autonomous: Reminder and status tracking for missing inputs runs on its own, and returned files are validated and merged automatically.
lenses.ambitious: A rolling quarterly reforecast instead of a yearly budget, which the business can trust because the actuals base is clean.
lenses.joy: No more copy-paste and version merges; the bookkeeper explains the cost base.
lenses.options: Prefill three baselines (last year, last 3 months annualised, contract-based) for managers to pick from.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper owns the actuals base and the mapping of accounts to budget lines.

tasks.human_edge: Knowing which past costs were one-offs and talking site managers through their numbers.
tasks.pattern_why: Actuals and mapping are structured; prefill, validation and merge can be built once.

in_practice.trigger: FP&A opens the budget or reforecast round.
steps: Prefill templates per site from AFAS actuals and the account mapping
Send templates and track returns
Validate returned files (totals, missing lines, out-of-range changes)
Merge into one file for FP&A
Bookkeeper reviews flagged lines with managers
in_practice.human_gate: Bookkeeper and FP&A review the merged file before it is used.
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint budget folder with versions and validation results

evidence.claim: Excel and Power Automate can prefill, distribute and validate budget templates.

risks: Prefilled numbers anchor managers and hide needed changes
Mapping errors spread to every template
Labour costs from the CAO round need HR input not in the actuals
research_questions: How many hours does the bookkeeping team spend per budget round, and on which steps?
Is the account to budget line mapping documented and stable?
Would FP&A accept a rolling reforecast fed by this pipeline?

tasks.short: Keep stock records of packaging, pallets, fuel and spare parts in AFAS in line with site counts.

today.trigger: Monthly stock counts from the three sites and pallet balance statements from pallet pools.
steps: Receive count sheets from sites (Excel or email)
Compare with AFAS stock or balance sheet values
Investigate differences with site staff
Post corrections and valuation changes
Reconcile pallet balances with customer and pool statements
drudgery: Retyping count sheets
Chasing sites for counts
Reconciling pallet exchange balances
today.time_sinks: Explaining count differences and pallet balance disputes.

lenses.faster: Sites submit counts in a fixed form; differences against AFAS calculate themselves.
lenses.autonomous: Count forms go out and are compared automatically; only differences above a threshold reach the bookkeeper.
lenses.ambitious: Monthly pallet balances agreed with every customer and pool, so pallet losses are charged instead of written off.
lenses.joy: No retyping count sheets; the work left is solving real differences.
lenses.options: Show each difference with possible causes (missed receipt, write-off, wrong unit).
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper owns thresholds, valuation rules and the count form.
reach: Controller: stock valuation for the close
Credit and Collections Officer: pallet charges to customers

tasks.human_edge: Working with site staff to find out what really happened to the stock.
tasks.pattern_why: Counts and book values are structured and differences are arithmetic.

steps: Send count form (Microsoft Forms or Excel on SharePoint)
Compare counts with AFAS values
Flag differences above threshold
Bookkeeper investigates and drafts corrections
Controller approves write-offs
in_practice.human_gate: Bookkeeper approves corrections; Controller approves write-offs above a limit.

evidence.claim: Standard form-based counts with automatic difference calculation are routine M365 work.

risks: Client-owned stock in the warehouse system gets mixed up with Noordhaven's own stock
Bad counts at source produce clean but wrong records
Small volumes may not justify building it
research_questions: Which stock does Noordhaven actually carry on its own balance sheet, and how much is it worth?
How many hours per month do stock and pallet reconciliations take?
Are pallet balances a material source of write-offs?

tasks.short: Prepare the VAT return, ICP listing, CBS statistics and g-rekening payments for agency invoices.

today.trigger: Monthly or quarterly filing deadlines and agency invoices with a wage tax and VAT share.
steps: Run the VAT report in AFAS
Check VAT codes on unusual postings and reverse-charge purchases
Prepare ICP and CBS figures
Split agency invoice amounts for the g-rekening
Hand to the Controller to sign and file
drudgery: Checking VAT codes line by line
Recomputing the g-rekening share per agency invoice
Collecting payment-behaviour statements from agencies
today.time_sinks: Finding wrong VAT codes and handling agency invoices that do not show the wage share.

lenses.faster: Rule checks flag wrong VAT codes, missing reverse-charge and g-rekening splits as invoices are booked, not at filing time.
lenses.autonomous: Agency invoices are checked against hours in the agency portal, the g-rekening share is split and the payment-behaviour statement expiry is tracked, with only differences to a person.
lenses.ambitious: Ready for the planned e-invoicing and transaction reporting (B2B from 2030, reporting from 2031), with purchases reported within days instead of at quarter end.
lenses.joy: No hunting for wrong VAT codes the night before the deadline.
lenses.options: Show filing-ready figures and a list of open risks per return, so the Controller decides what to correct first.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper owns VAT code rules, the g-rekening checks and the filing calendar.
reach: Payroll Specialist: pension and wage tax checks on agency labour

tasks.human_edge: Interpreting VAT treatment of unusual transactions and signing responsibility toward the Belastingdienst.
tasks.pattern_why: VAT codes, reverse-charge rules and the g-rekening split are written-down rules on structured AFAS data; filing stays with a person.

in_practice.trigger: Each booked purchase and sales invoice, plus filing calendar dates.
steps: Rule checks on VAT code, country and reverse charge at booking
Agency invoice hours checked against the portal; g-rekening share split into the payment run
Track validity of agency payment-behaviour statements
Generate VAT and ICP figures with an exception list
Controller reviews and files
in_practice.human_gate: Controller reviews and submits every return; bookkeeper approves VAT code corrections.
in_practice.logs_to: Tax file in SharePoint with exception list, corrections and filed return

evidence.claim: Hirers can be held liable for agencies' unpaid wage tax and VAT and can limit this with a payment-behaviour statement, record keeping and g-rekening payments.
The Dutch government chose to introduce B2B e-invoicing from 1 July 2030 and reporting from 1 July 2031; not yet law.
Under ViDA, buyers may need to report intra-EU and reverse-charge purchases within 5 days of receipt.

risks: Rule table outdated after a VAT change leads to wrong returns
Agency invoices without a clear wage share make the split a guess
Liability stays with Noordhaven whatever the tool does
research_questions: How many VAT corrections were made in the last four returns and what caused them?
Do all three agencies show the wage share and hours in a form that can be checked automatically?
How long does each return take today from report to filing?

role.altitude: From keying, matching and reconciling to owning the match rules, tolerances, VAT codes, supplier and customer master data, and the exception queue that AFAS and the checks produce.
reach: Credit and Collections Officer: early dispute and part-payment signals from bank matching
Controller: close readiness checks and trial balance review
FP&A Analyst: clean actuals base and budget prefill
Payroll Specialist: checks on agency labour invoices and g-rekening
role.ceiling_note: Limited by data quality (PDF invoices, missing payment references, agency invoices without wage share), by AFAS configuration being owned by a few people, and by sign-off duties: payments, write-offs and tax filings stay with named people. Roughly 40 to 70 percent of hours on these tasks can go; the rest is exceptions and judgment.
skills_to_grow: Designing and testing AFAS match rules and tolerances
Power BI report building on the AFAS extract
Writing check rules and reviewing exception rates
Reviewing LLM extraction output and spotting failure patterns
role.ambitious_version: The three bookkeepers run a daily soft close: bank, AP and AR clear every morning, only exceptions reach a person, agency invoices are checked against hours with the g-rekening split automatic, and Noordhaven is ready for e-invoicing well before 2030, cutting days to close and audit adjustments.
